content:
I have a slightly pedantic request/proposal for Mathlib dependency and toolchain bumps: adaptations for dependencies (batteries, etc.) should be included in the PRs reported at #nightly-testing-mathlib > Mathlib `lake update` failure, while nightly-testing and toolchain bumps should purely be for adaptations for core Lean.

The reason this is important to me is that when you are further downstream of Mathlib, it is much nicer to have a clear delineation in the git history between these different kinds of changes. As an example, for the most recent toolchain bump this was not the case, as #42604 included adaptations for batteries. While it is still possible to find the corresponding change in batteries, it is much nicer to do so from the lake update PRs where not every git revision is changing at the same time.

To be clear: this requires no change to any existing CI, just that whoever is making the dependency adaptations adds their commit to the automatically opened lake update PR, which I believe is already their intended usage. Changes for dependencies go here, and the nightly testing CI will automatically then pull these in and leave only failures from core.
I guess you're proposing that people making adaptations make PRs into the update-dependencies-bot-use-only branch (if it exists) rather than master?

Yes. In practice I imagined that it is a maintainer making these changes that would have permission to push to this PR directly. Using this existing mechanism seemed reasonable to me, but isn't as important as generally not mixing dependency adaptations into nightly testing/toolchain bumps.

So looking into #42604 specifically, from #ecosystem infrastructure > downstream-lean4 breakages @ 💬 it looks like there were adaptations for batteries#1831 in a batteries-pr-testing branch which never got PR'd to mathlib4 before the bump deadline.

Yes, there is discussion above that at #ecosystem infrastructure > downstream-lean4 breakages @ 💬. I personally would have chosen to have this PR'd separately beforehand (by whatever mechanism) rather than combining into the toolchain PR.

Again the pedantic aspect is that either way we end up with the same result for the new toolchain. But (in my view) it makes the scope of nightly testing less clear, combines unrelated changes, and leaves more of a puzzle to unravel for downstream users that may not watch Zulip as closely.

By the way, whose responsibility is it to make adaptation PRs? I mentioned in the description and in a comment of batteries#1831 that there were some adaptations on the testing branch that were not in mathlib, and that I'd be happy to make such a PR if necessary, but wasn't sure what automation took care of and what it didn't. (I didn't receive a response before it was merged.)

In general, should the PR authors make the adaptation PRs?
I think so, but I don't think we have a policy written down anywhere yet.
There's a large section in batteries' README.md

Relevant excerpt:

When necessary, Batteries contributors are expected to either create an adaptation PR on Mathlib, or ask for assistance... create an adaptation PR on Mathlib from the batteries-pr-testing-N branch

Well, I guess that's on me. It didn't occur to me to look there, as it's not the sort of information I'd expect to find in a README. (Perhaps most would, but I didn't! :upside_down:) It's still unfortunate that I mentioned this a couple times on the PR itself and it got merged, though :/ Should there perhaps be a label indicating whether adaptations are necessary, or demanding an adaptations PR be linked if there are nontrivial commits on the testing branch? ...This may be too difficult to be worth the time setting it up, I'm not sure.

The README does also say:

Once the Mathlib adaptation PR and the original Batteries PR have been reviewed and accepted, the Batteries PR will be merged first.

which suggests that a reviewer should check this is happening in tandem. Maybe it was assumed that since the adaptation branch was passing that it would get PR'd. (There are also a lot of moving pieces lately with nightly testing, so I think it's reasonable for there to be a little confusion!)

This is a bit distinct from my original question, but ultimately related. The letter of this policy makes it clear that this should happen in its own PR to Mathlib, not be added to Mathlib nightly-testing. I would be happy for this to be strictly followed in practice.
